The proof is valid: evaluate global support at x+g to obtain ||g||^2<=f(x+g)-f(x), then apply Lipschitz growth to bound the same increment by G||g||. If g=0, nonnegativity of G closes the claim; otherwise norm positivity permits division and gives ||g||<=G. No support-existence or finite-dimensional compactness argument is used.

Its failed global test point x+g=-1 is outside C. This refutes the constrained variant without contradicting the global theorem.

Zero and nonunit finite masses are admitted. At mu=0 the integrated identity is zero=zero, even though the selected condDistrib remains a pointwise mass-one Markov kernel. Modifying a measurable conditional version on a mu_1-null set does not affect its integrated identity; it does not determine conditional support or convergence behavior at exceptional starting inputs.

The proposed finite example is valid: beta is a singleton and alpha has two states with uniform first marginal, so every update is the identity. Starting from the first state's Dirac law leaves that law fixed and its total variation distance from the uniform target equals one-half for all n>=0. Thus this invariant target is not a convergence guarantee from a law with another first marginal. This is not a claim that the heat-bath kernel is nonreversible; reversibility is simply not this target conclusion.
